title: Concurrent streaming emulator for SSE/WebSocket with p95 regression detection
creator: Aisha Kulkarni
description: Build a horizontally scalable streaming load emulator ("stream-emulator") that can simulate realistic chat/completions traffic over both Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSocket transports. The harness will measure tokens/sec, per-message latencies (p50/p95/p99), connection churn, and error profiles at scale, and will include automated regression detection against a golden baseline. Goals: 1) reproduce production-like concurrency and token distributions, 2) provide deterministic, CI-friendly regressions for p95 and tokens/sec, 3) integrate output with Grafana/Alerting and CI pipelines for automatic gate checks.
acceptance_criteria: Emulator can spawn 100k concurrent simulated streams across multiple k8s worker pods and maintain at least 10k active concurrent streams for 10 minutes without driver OOM.
Captures tokens/sec with end-to-end accounting (client-reported + server-confirmed) and reports per-second tokens/sec timeseries to Prometheus/Grafana.
p95 generation latency measured per logical response (end-to-end) and stored as histogram metrics (prometheus_summary or histogram buckets) and exported as JSON for CI comparisons.

Regression detection job runs in CI: compares current run to golden baseline and fails when p95 latency increases by >= 5% with statistical significance (bootstrap resampling, p < 0.05) or when tokens/sec drops by >= 7%.
Supports both SSE and WebSocket modes with identical measurement semantics and an option to enable simulated network jitter/packet-loss (configurable percentages).
Produces CI-artifact JSON and CSV with per-run summary: tokens_total, tokens_per_second_peak, p50, p95, p99, connection_errors, send_retries, and raw latency samples (compressed).
Dashboards created with panels for tokens/sec, p95/p99, connection errors, and per-region rollup; alerts configured for regression thresholds and rising error rates.
implementation_plan: Design: finalize emulator API and config format (client profiles, token distribution, inter-message delays, transport mode). See design doc link.
Core emulator: implement in Go for lightweight concurrency; use goroutines with bounded worker pools and configurable backpressure; WebSocket via gorilla/websocket, SSE via chunked HTTP responses.
Measurement: instrument client and server sides; include deterministic token counting library to normalize across tokenizer variants; emit Prometheus metrics and JSON artifacts.
Scaling: package as k8s Job + HPA-friendly Deployment; driver pod runs coordinator, workers run as sidecar or separate pods; include an autoscaler profile for test clouds.

Regression detection: implement a small analysis binary that performs bootstrap comparison to golden baseline stored in s3 and returns non-zero on failure; integrate step into GitHub Actions and Concourse pipelines.
Integrations: wire metrics into existing runtime Grafana dashboards; create a daily scheduled full-scale run that archives artifacts, and a PR gate that runs a lightweight smoke against the emulator.
Runbook & safety: add circuit-breaker to stop runs when error rate exceeds threshold; add quota protections to prevent accidental production traffic against hosted endpoints.

notes_and_tradeoffs: Using Go keeps binary small and CPU efficient, but stellar concurrency will rely on careful GC tuning; we may need to pin GOGC on driver pods.
Simulating production prompts precisely (token distribution) requires a canonical tokenizer; until that's settled we will normalize by whitespace-token counts as an interim approach.
Full-scale runs are expensive; plan to maintain a small nightly benchmark and an on-demand large-scale run for releases only.
Statistical regression detection prefers bootstrap sampling for small sample stability; this is slower but more robust to heavy-tailed latency distributions than simple delta checks.
